rulings.rationale: The OBS-007 decisions removed the account machinery (EXT-001 dropped; the v3 AdmissionRequest is closed; secrets resolve at dispatch, not admission; preflight reads names only). Each is equal or stronger. No compatibility shim was added to keep the old names green, which D-A requires.

subRulings.ruling: D-A residue with an integrity weakness. Assigned to STUDIO-OBS-014: delete it; do not guard it.

verified: The runner's only admission call is /observed-admission (studio-runner/src/reporting/admissionClient.ts:65). No runner code calls /admission. Its only caller was the /v1/runs path that AC-3 deleted.

admit() is a CAS on studio_dispatch_ledger (state DISPATCHING, admission_id NULL, deadline, not cancelled) with no observed-receipt or binding check. claim() never calls ObservedReplayAuthorization.check(binding); claimObserved does (AdmissionCasService:133-214).
inferred: Every Studio execution is observed now, so the legacy route can only ever admit an observed row while bypassing binding authorization. exec-fixtures saw that the genuine observed admission is then refused ADMISSION_OWNED. It releases no secret, because secrets are resolved and sent at dispatch, which R3 now rechecks.

subRulings.rationale: Guarding the route would add a branch that can never succeed, which is a compatibility shim. Deletion is the D-A answer. It belongs in OBS-014 (security P0/P1, starts immediately after 012A, already touches internal routes), not OBS-011, which runs after OBS-010 release. Fixing in 012A was weighed and rejected: no untrusted caller can reach the route, the outcome is fail-closed, and the fix would void run5b and the in-flight runner tiers for no risk reduction before 013/014 start. rulings.topic: Chrome for Testing startup hang (run4-residual item 2; reconciliation G-8)
rulings.ruling: Does not block 012A. Product ownership: STUDIO-OBS-009. Test-infra ownership: STUDIO-OBS-009 AC-12. Host cleanup: user (G4).

verified: 012A did not touch the guided launch: guidedMain.ts is byte-identical to T0, and the 012A delta in browser.ts is a removed type import (runner-gates R4_C3 versusBaseline).

launchGuidedBrowser (browser.ts:533) calls chromium.launchPersistentContext with no Studio-owned timeout, and none of the boundedStartup wrapping the replay path uses (browser.ts:140-158). Installed playwright-core sets DEFAULT_PLAYWRIGHT_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT = 180 s (coreBundle.js:4595). So the launch is not literally unbounded, but its only bound is a third-party default 12x the Java 15 s pushContext deadline.
The replay path's launcher spawns the child as its own process group and kills the tree (launcher.ts:238-299). The guided worker launches Chromium in-process and has no equivalent group.
Run5b: GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest 40/40, GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest 37/37. Two checks-guided-* processes are still alive on the host.
inferred: The deadlock is in Chromium's fork child handler (xpc_atfork_child), not in repository code. The orphans survive because the IT force-kills the node worker before Playwright's 180 s launch timeout could reap the group.

rulings.rationale: The failure is fail-closed: no bootstrap callback is sent, the API side is bounded at 15 s, and nothing is learned or published. Adding a launch bound is a runner product timeout change and belongs where the guided worker becomes the one runner process (ADR-SC-005 placement: one runner process/image is OBS-009). There it should adopt the replay path's discipline: a process group per browser, a Studio-owned startup deadline at or below the guided bootstrap budget, and tree reaping on kill (same family as R10-OBS-1, already OBS-009 AC-11 j).

rulings.topic: Host-port collision class (run4 Zonky; run5 Docker *:P shadowed by a stale Gradle daemon's 127.0.0.1:P listener)
rulings.ruling: Yes. Record it as a standing test-infra risk with a classification rule. The product fix is complete (LocalEmbeddedPostgresConfig). The residual is environmental and is placed in STUDIO-OBS-009 AC-12 plus the root Gradle wrapper preflight.

verified: The LocalEmbeddedPostgresConfig fix (20000-32767, dual-stack exclusive probe) has LocalEmbeddedPostgresPortTest 3/3, and OptimisticSaveIT/ObservedReadEntryProtocolIT 3x green (run4-residual). Run5b green.
The run5 cause is still present now: PID 33891 LISTENs on 127.0.0.1:52100.

rulings.rationale: On macOS/BSD a more specific 127.0.0.1:P or ::1:P listener shadows Docker Desktop's *:P for loopback clients. Any stale local JVM or postgres in the ephemeral range can therefore redirect a Testcontainers JDBC connection. Symptoms: EOFException at connect, `role "test" does not exist`, or a hang. CI agents are ephemeral, so the risk lives mainly on developer and agent hosts. The remaining in-repo latent hazard is GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest RUNNER_PORT via ServerSocket(0) with a 127.0.0.1-only readiness probe.
